method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Sheet 54 prints '26TH ST' along its top edge and '27TH ST.' along its bottom with the adjoining-sheet numeral '60' set in the corridor; sheet 60 prints '27TH ST.' along its top with the adjoining numeral '54', and '28TH ST.' lower down. The avenue-frontage hundred-block steps at exactly that line: sheet 54's blocks carry the 2600 runs (2601 2603 ... 2627 / 2602 2604 ... 2628, and 2601-2628 again on the Ave R block 'N.W. 141'), sheet 60's carry the 2700 runs (2701 2703 ... 2731 / 2702 2704 ... 2732) and then 2801-2806 south of 28th. The 27th St frontage runs face each other across the corridor: 2201 2203 2205 2207 2209 2211 and 2213 2215 2217 2219 2221 2223 on sheet 54's south block faces, the same 2201-2211 / 2213-2223 and 2301-2311 on sheet 60's north faces. Block halves also match up - 'N.W. 116' and 'S.W. 116' on sheet 54 against 'N.E. 115' and 'S.E. 115' plus 'N.E. 140' on sheet 60. Scale: 28th St is drawn 243 native px wide on sheet 60 with '80' printed in it, so a numbered street is 80 ft = 243 px and the block between 27th and 28th measures 902 px = 297 ft (~300 ft, matching sheet 54's 907 px between 26th and 27th). Sheet 54's north face of 27th St is at native y 3614, centre 3735; sheet 60's south face at native y 347, centre 226. Detection candidates 3275 (sheet 54) and 904 (sheet 60) both fell inside blocks.
